title: A high-throughput DNA FISH protocol to visualize genome regions in human cells
protocol: Dilute DNAse in PCR-grade water 1:1000 to a final concentration of 1 μg/mL.
Retest the diluted DNAse with known probes every time a fresh DNAse stock is opened.
Dilute DNA to 65 μg/ml in PCR-grade water on ice by mixing 1 μg probe DNA and filling up to 15.5 μl with PCR-grade water.
Mix master mix (scaled up as necessary) on ice and protected from light: 2.5 μL 10× nick translation buffer
Mix 2.5 μL of fluorescent nucleotide stock with each reaction tube.
Add 2.5 μL of β-mercaptoethanol to each reaction tube.
Pipette 1 μL of diluted DNAse stock into each reaction tube.
Add 1 μL of DNA polymerase to each reaction tube.
Add 9.5 μL of master mix per 2 μg probe DNA to each reaction tube.
Tap tubes to remove bubbles and spin for 1 min at 20,000 g in a desktop centrifuge.
Incubate the tubes at 16°C in a water bath in a cold room for 80 min.
Add 1 μL of 0.5 M EDTA to stop the reaction.
Incubate at 72°C for 10 min after adding EDTA.
Run 5 μL of the reaction volume on a 2% agarose gel at 60 V for 30 min as a quality control step.
Verify that probes run as a smear between 100 bp and 1000 bp.
Mix 20 μL nick translated probe in each color being used.
Add 9 μL human Cot-1 DNA (competitor; final concentration: 25 ng/μL).
Add 6 μL yeast tRNA (carrier; final concentration: 165 ng/μL).
Add 12 μL NaOAc.
Add 150 μL ethanol to the mixture.
Vortex to mix thoroughly.
Spin for 1 minute at 20,000 g in a desktop centrifuge.
Chill at −20°C for 60 minutes.
Spin at 4°C at 20,000 g for 30 minutes.
Gently decant the supernatant and air dry tubes while inverted and protected from light for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in an appropriate solution.
Add 45 μL hybridization buffer to the resuspended pellet.
Heat to 65°C and vortex, or use a thermomixer at 65°C and 700+ rpm for at least 60 minutes.
Fix cells directly from cell culture.
Add 50 μL 8% PFA in PBS to wells already containing cells and 50 μL media (final: 100 μL of 4% PFA in PBS).
Incubate 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse thrice in PBS.
Incubate cells in permeabilization solution for 20 min at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse cells twice in PBS.
Denature cells in 0.1N HCl for 15 min at 20°C–22°C.
Neutralize cells in 2× SSC for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Incubate cells in equilibration buffer for at least 30 min at 20°C–22°C.
Combine the probe with the cells.
Allow stable binding of the probe to the cells.
Wash off excess probe before imaging.
Aspirate equilibration buffer gently from wells using a 200 μL micropipette.
Add 13.5 μL of probe mix to each well.
Do not let the cells get dry at any point during this step.
Seal the plate with foil to block light and prevent evaporation.
Tap the plate firmly against the benchtop to disrupt bubbles.
Spin the plate for 1 minute at least at 100 g in a plate centrifuge.
Denature by placing plate directly onto preheated slide moat at 85°C for 7.5 min.
Ensure all wells are fully in contact with the metal surface of the slide moat.
Immediately move to humid hybridization chamber at 37°C and hybridize for at least 18 h.
Rinse once in 2× SSC at 20°C–22°C.
Wash three times for 5 min in 1× SSC at 42°C.
Wash three times for 5 min in 0.1× SSC at 42°C.
Stain with DAPI.
Dilute DAPI in PBS.
Incubate for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse once with PBS.
Plate with PBS, seal plate with foil.
If stored at 4°C prior to imaging, warm plate at 20°C–22°C for one hour or at 37°C for 15 min to prevent condensation on the bottom of the plate.
Clean the bottom of the plate with 70% ethanol.
Load the plate into the microscope.
Find the approximate focal plane and height of the cells in the DAPI channel.
Verify the signal-to-noise ratio in all channels used: DAPI should be at least 5:1, and FISH signals should be easily discernible.
Program in the following image acquisition steps.
Set each channel’s acquisition to unbinned with the same z-stack centered around the determined software focus.
Optimize the laser power and exposure time for good signal-to-noise ratios (3-fold is ideal) without oversaturating the signal.
Optimize the DAPI channel focus within a 10 μm z-stack surrounding the approximate focal plane found in step 32.
Acquire DAPI images (Excitation: 405 nm, Emission: 445/50).
Acquire Dyomics DY488 or another green fluorophore image (Excitation: 488 nm, Emission: 525/50).
Acquire Dyomics DY549P1 or another red fluorophore image (Excitation: 561 nm, Emission: 600/27).
Select Dyomics DY647P1 or another deep red fluorophore for acquisition (Ex: 640, Em: 676/29).
Consider the z-slicing interval based on whether data will be analyzed in 2D or 3D.
For 2D analysis, use a z-slice interval around 1 μm to match the depth of field of the lens.
For 3D analysis, recommend an oversampling in z by at least 3-fold (i.e., a z-slice interval around 300 nm).
Verify imaging conditions in at least 5–10 wells if different probes are used across the plate.
Program the microscope to acquire fields of view sufficient to image 1,000 cells per condition.
Save and launch the routine for data acquisition.
